record.original_question: Consider P||C_max on parallel identical machines with high-multiplicity encoding, where there are p distinct processing times and both the processing-time values and the counts of jobs of each type are encoded in binary. Is this problem fixed-parameter tractable when parameterized by p?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 5. Is P||Cmax with high-multiplicity encoding fixed-parameter tractable parameterized by the number p of distinct processing times, that is, when job processing times pj and the number of jobs for each processing time are encoded in binary?

Parallel identical machines (denoted by “P” in the α-field). We are given a number m of parallel identical machines (that is, of the same speed). Each job j has to be processed by exactly one machine for a given amount pj ∈ N of time and each machine can process only one job at a time.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the makespan minimization problem on parallel identical machines, denoted P||C_max, defined as follows. We are given a positive integer m (the number of identical machines) and a multiset of n jobs, where each job j has a processing time p_j ∈ ℕ. A schedule assigns each job to exactly one machine; each machine processes its assigned jobs sequentially without preemption, and the makespan is the maximum, over all machines, of the total processing time of jobs assigned to that machine. The goal is to minimize the makespan.

Assume the input is given in high-multiplicity binary encoding: there are p distinct processing times t_1, …, t_p ∈ ℕ, and for each i ∈ {1, …, p} a multiplicity n_i ∈ ℕ specifying that there are n_i jobs of processing time t_i. Both the values t_i and the multiplicities n_i are encoded in binary, so the total input size is O(p · (log max_i t_i + log max_i n_i) + log m).

Question: Is this problem fixed-parameter tractable when parameterized by p? Equivalently, does there exist a computable function f and a constant c such that the problem can be solved in time f(p) · ⟨I⟩^c, where ⟨I⟩ is the binary input length?
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work (2024–2025) on high-multiplicity scheduling explicitly refers to this as a major open question of Mnich and van Bevern, and shows it is equivalent to the analogous question for Q||C_max, but does not resolve it. ETH-tight FPT algorithms exist when one additionally parameterizes by the maximum processing time, but FPT-tractability parameterized solely by the number of distinct processing times under binary high-multiplicity encoding remains open.

status_evidence.title: Exact and Approximate High-Multiplicity Scheduling on Identical Machines
status_evidence.snippet: the big open question asked by Mnich and van Bevern...whether P||C_max is FPT w.r.t. the number of job types d has the same answer as the question whether Q||C_max is FPT
status_evidence.claim: The paper establishes an equivalence to another open problem but does not resolve FPT-tractability of P||C_max parameterized by the number of job types in high-multiplicity encoding.

status_evidence.title: ETH-Tight FPT Algorithm for Makespan Minimization on Uniform Machines
status_evidence.snippet: makespan minimization parameterized by the maximum processing time and the number of distinct processing times d, in time p_max^O(d) · n^O(1)
status_evidence.claim: FPT results are known when also parameterizing by p_max, but parameterization by p alone with binary encoding is not resolved.
